structured_output.summary: Add a pure ASGI RequestBodyLimitMiddleware that keeps shared limit state in the scope so inner Route/Mount/Router limits can override the outer one. Make the multipart parser close temp files on any interruption. Then wire max_body_size into Router/Mount/Route and into Starlette's middleware stack. Four tasks; docs are not added.

intents.rationale: New module starlette/middleware/body_limit.py does not exist yet.
Content-Length fail-fast plus received-byte counting is implemented in the new middleware.
The middleware tracks whether response.start was sent. If it was, it sends no 413, and the receive wrapper still raises to stop the stream.
None of Starlette, Router, Mount or Route accepts max_body_size today.
Starlette inserts the middleware before user middleware. Route, Mount and Router wrap their app with the middleware, which updates the shared limit already in scope.

evidence.quote: for cls, args, kwargs in reversed(middleware):

intents.rationale: Cleanup only happens for MultiPartException and OSError. It must cover every exception, including a body-limit error raised from the stream.
New and extended tests are needed.

criteria.text: A body larger than max_body_size, with or without Content-Length, gets a plain-text 413 'Content Too Large' response; streaming bodies and multipart uploads are counted by received bytes including encoding overhead.
A declared Content-Length over the limit is rejected with 413 before the app reads the body. An understated Content-Length does not bypass the limit. A body exactly at the limit succeeds.
If the app already sent http.response.start when the limit is crossed, the middleware sends no second response, and the receive call still raises or terminates.
Starlette, Router, Mount and Route accept max_body_size (default None, unlimited) and enforce it.
The app-level limit applies to application middleware that reads the body. An inner Route, Mount or Router limit can raise or lower the outer limit after routing.
When multipart parsing is interrupted by any exception, including one raised mid-stream by the body limit, every temporary file created is closed.
Nothing new is exported from the starlette package root; the middleware is imported from starlette.middleware.body_limit.

tasks.summary: Create RequestBodyLimitMiddleware. It stores shared state in scope (limit, received count, response-started flag), so a nested instance overrides the limit instead of double counting. It does the Content-Length fail-fast check, counts received bytes, sends a plain-text 413 only if no response has started, and always raises or stops the receive stream.
In MultiPartParser.parse, close the tracked temp files on any exception (use except BaseException or a finally flag) and re-raise. Add tests with a stream that raises mid-upload.
Add keyword max_body_size: int | None = None to Route, Mount and Router. When not None, wrap the app (or the Router middleware stack) in RequestBodyLimitMiddleware so it overrides any outer limit.

Add max_body_size to Starlette. Insert the middleware in build_middleware_stack after ServerErrorMiddleware and before user middleware. Pass the limit so the Starlette-level limit is the one in scope before routing. Test an inner Route, Mount or Router raising or lowering the limit, and user middleware reading the body.
